title: pm-dispatch: tier the governed surface — the rules layer stays hand-merged, `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/**` lands through the queue after in-seat contract-tier review (maintainer ruling 2026-09-13)
body:
Filed by the `domain:skills` seat (session `session_01DAcomhvR9kKizeYgg89Vo8`, GitHub `os-project-manager`) at 2026-09-13T07:49Z, routed and graded into this lane under the maintainer's 2026-09-13 self-routing ruling (recorded on #17942). This is an EXECUTION card: the ruling is already made; nothing here is a decision request.

## The ruling (live chat with this seat, 2026-09-13T07:2xZ–07:4xZ, verbatim, untranslated)

Maintainer: 「③ 受管面手合本身也是一条队列。能否简化我的审核步骤,比如我召唤项目总监时可以批量决定?」
Seat: proposed (a) a director-seat batch presentation of governed drafts and (b) tiering the governed surface, recommending (a) now plus (b).
Maintainer: 「收窄受管面,但是 skills 是不是还是应该我来确认?」
Seat, the boundary put to the maintainer, verbatim:
> **规则层(你确认)**:所有 SKILL.md 级的规则文本——发布的 `skills/**`(两个仓)、`.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md`(含 pm-dispatch 本体和内部 playbook)、`core-rules.md`、`.claude/agents/**`、hooks、settings、`AGENTS.md`、`CLAUDE.md`、ADR。
> **事实层(席内契约复审档复核后入队)**:只有 `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/**`——平台读数表、runbook、契约复核细则、车道文件、状态机细则。
Maintainer: 「我点头」

⇒ Ruled: published `skills/**` (both repos), every `.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md`, `core-rules.md`, `.claude/agents/**`, `.claude/hooks/**`, `.claude/settings*`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` and `docs/adr/**` keep the human hand merge exactly as today. **Only `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/**` changes**: a PR whose governed paths are all under that directory lands through the merge queue after the skills seat's in-seat contract-tier review (served tier verified per `references/contract-review.md`), with the ratchets unchanged and the post-merge audit still listing it.

## Governing text

- `AGENTS.md` Prime Directive #14: the governed surfaces are named there and 「The register is the `GOVERNED_SURFACES` table in `scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs`; adding a surface is an edit *there*, never here, and `pnpm check:pm-governed-prose` reds per-PR when this paragraph names fewer surfaces than the register — or more.」
- `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md` 〈复核〉: 「governed 面统一定义:`docs/adr/**` + `.claude/**`(全量,含 agents/hooks/settings)+ `skills/**`」 and 「路径面一条命中 ⇒ ACCEPT 换终局四件套」.
- `references/contract-review.md`: 「受管面人工合并 ⛔ 不替代复核,两道保障叠加」 and 落地前检③ 「受管面不适用,draft-only 终局不变」.
- `references/lanes/skills.md` 常设承诺: 「受管面 PR 恒 draft 等人合;flip 或 arm 前跑 `check-governed-merges --test` 带路径」.
- The queue guard: `scripts/pm/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs` (`Governed Surface Queue Guard`, the seventh required context) refuses an unpinned governed diff in the merge group; `GOVERNED_APPROVERS` lives there.

## Work items (one PR; it touches `AGENTS.md` and `SKILL.md`, so it is itself hand-merged by the maintainer)

1. `scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs`: the register distinguishes LANDING from AUDIT — the `.claude/**` row keeps auditing everything under `.claude/`, but `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/**` is marked as landing through the queue after seat review (a per-row landing field, or a carve-out row — the dev measures which shape the existing `--test` / `--pr` / `--branch` readers and the self-test support with the smallest diff). `--test` on a references path prints a verdict that names the tier; `--test` on `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md`, `.claude/skills/spec-property-retirement/SKILL.md`, `.claude/agents/os-dev.md`, `.claude/hooks/*.sh`, `AGENTS.md`, `docs/adr/*.md`, `skills/**` stays GOVERNED. Self-test cases in both directions.
2. `scripts/pm/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs`: the merge-group leg reads the same predicate (import, not a copy) so a references-only diff passes the queue without an authorized approval, and a mixed diff (references plus any rules-layer path) stays refused. Self-test both directions. objectui's `scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs`: measure whether objectui has any `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/` path at all; if none, no change there — say so.
3. `AGENTS.md` Prime Directive #14 paragraph: name the carve-out in one sentence so `check:pm-governed-prose` stays green (measure it before and after; the gate's own rule is the authority on what the paragraph must name).
4. `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md` 〈复核〉 governed-face definition line and the ACCEPT fork; `references/contract-review.md` 落地前检③; `references/lanes/skills.md` 常设承诺 — each states the tier in one clause: references-only PRs = in-seat contract-tier review (served tier verified) → ready → auto-merge / queue; everything else unchanged. All at ceiling (812 / 60 / lane file) ⇒ paid by density, ⛔ re-wrap is not currency, ⛔ no ceiling raise.
5. The round report's governed-merge audit section keeps listing references merges (with `merged_by`), so the maintainer still sees every one after the fact.

## Acceptance

- `node scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs --test .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/platform-readings.md` ⇒ a verdict that says the path lands through the queue after seat review (NOT the GOVERNED / human-merge verdict); the same command on `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md` ⇒ GOVERNED (unchanged). Both quoted in the PR body.
- Queue-guard self-test: a references-only fixture passes with zero approvals; a references-plus-`SKILL.md` fixture is refused; the existing fixtures unchanged.
- `pnpm check:pm-governed-prose` green on the branch; `pnpm check:pm-skill-ratchet` green (no ceiling moved); `pnpm check:pm-governed-merges` self-test green.
- The audit (`check-governed-merges.mjs --since-ref …`) still lists a references-only merge — shown by running it over a window that contains one (e.g. PR #17823 / #17828 of 2026-09-12) with the row present.

## Not in scope

- ⛔ Published `skills/**` in either repo: stays the maintainer's, by the maintainer's own word.
- ⛔ Any other surface, any change to `GOVERNED_APPROVERS`, any change to the ratchets.
- The director-seat batch presentation of governed drafts is its own card (filed alongside this one).

## Why p1

Maintainer-directed; today two of the five drafts waiting on the maintainer in this lane alone (PR #17803, PR #17515) are references-plus-script diffs, and references rows were the majority of this lane's hand-merged PRs on 2026-09-11 / 09-12 — the single human terminal is the longest queue in the lane.
